findings.description: Static AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded as Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. Anyone with read access to the repo, the Terraform state, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can retrieve these long-lived credentials and impersonate the IAM principal.

The function's environment variables (which hold secrets) are not encrypted with a customer-managed CMK because kms_key_arn is unset, so they are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are visible in plaintext to any caller able to describe the function.
The function uses nodejs12.x, an end-of-life Lambda runtime that no longer receives security patches, leaving known vulnerabilities in the runtime unaddressed.
No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so Lambda does not verify that the deployment package is signed by a trusted publisher, allowing tampered or malicious code to be deployed.
